population.note: FICTIONAL. Out of about 274M adults, 28.5% are current users (≈78.1M) and 40.0% have ever used (≈109.6M). That leaves 11.5% (≈31.5M) who used and are off now, and ≈164M who have never used. Cycling arithmetic: ever 40.0 − current 28.5 = 11.5 pts off now. About 14.5 pts of current users are on a second or later course, and about 4.5 pts of the off-now group restarted at least once and stopped again, so (14.5 + 4.5)/40.0 ≈ 47.5% have cycled. That fits ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart within a year. The 2033 pen recall and shortage forced about 2M temporary stops, and most of those people restarted on the 50 mg pill or on imports. Ever-use rose 4.5 pts (limit 6.5) and current use rose 3.5. Age check: 18–29: 15.5% × 52M = 8.1M; 30–49: 32% × 91M = 29.1M; 50–64: 42.5% × 62M = 26.4M; 65+: 21% × 69M = 14.5M. Total ≈ 78.1M = 28.5%. Income thirds average (32 + 29 + 24.5)/3 = 28.5. Bottom-third growth is mostly imports: ≈7.1M imported or counterfeit users, up from 3.8M, concentrated in non-expansion states and among workers waiting out employer tenure gates. Top-third growth comes from MariTide and from 12 mg retatrutide coming off allocation. The 65+ band rose more slowly (17→21%) because roughly one in five older ever-users is on a medically advised bone pause or a post-NAION stop. The ≈164M never-users are skewed toward under-30s, rural residents of non-expansion states, people with contraindications, and refusers by conviction. Pediatric use is 1.0% of ≈73M ≈ 730k, mostly adolescents 12+ on Medicaid EPSDT and commercial plans; the adolescent bone readout is unresolved. About two children in five now live with at least one parent who is on the drug or cycling off it.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. The statutory terms of the permanent Part D obesity benefit are unchanged: $199/month negotiated rate, $50 copay, counselling visit, eligibility at BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity. The 50 mg Wegovy pill was added to Part D formularies at the statutory rate in Apr 2034. Medicare pays 18.5% of fills, ≈14.4M users (≈13.1M aged 65+ and ≈1.3M disabled under-65): ≈6.4M for diabetes and ≈8.0M for obesity. Obesity-benefit spend: 8.0M × $199 × 12 ≈ $19.1B gross. Beneficiaries pay 8.0M × $50 × 12 ≈ $4.8B, leaving ≈$14.3B for the program. All Medicare incretin fills: 14.4M × $199 × 12 ≈ $34.4B gross. Medicaid: 31 states plus DC still use the 90% match and the continuation standard, and no state joined or left. Medicaid pays 14.7% of fills, ≈11.5M users × $199 × 12 ≈ $27.5B gross before supplemental rebates. Because public rates are fixed while cash and commercial prices rose, manufacturers recover margin from private payers.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $5–30/month, including generic oral semaglutide. The first US-filer's Telangana sterile plant is under a US import alert but still supplies the Indian domestic market and, indirectly, parcel traffic. China: domestic generic semaglutide, tirzepatide copies, and 'research-grade' retatrutide vials, with Chinese API still underlying most of the gray trade. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 50–80/month. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt also have generics. US: the 2033 generic semaglutide entry did not happen. The first filer's 180-day exclusivity is 'parked' behind an FDA warning letter, and the settlement's contingent date for other filers is mid-2035. Tirzepatide exclusivity runs later.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Shock up. After the Aug 2033 pen recall and a 5-month FDA shortage listing, and with the 2029 portal price commitments expired, Novo and Lilly raised direct-portal maintenance prices by about $50. Current prices: injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide $249–329; Wegovy pill 50 mg $299 direct; oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) still $149–150; retatrutide $449 direct and $1,649 list; amycretin $499; MariTide $549/month-equivalent direct. PBM net rose to ≈$195–215. Payer mix of ≈78.0M users: commercial 37.2% (29.0M); Medicare 18.5% (14.4M); Medicaid 14.7% (11.5M); cash/direct 20.5% (16.0M, including ≈4.6M 'calm' and 'focus' subscribers); imported/counterfeit 9.1% (7.1M). Sum = 78.0M = 100%. About 85% of covering employers now use gated designs, and about a third of those add tenure gates. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand. Routes: ≈36% of users are on daily orals, up from ≈27%, as pill parity and the pen shortage pushed switching.

smoking and vaping cessation (no resubmission yet)
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens in concierge practices

gray-market 'research' retatrutide among gym and physique users
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The oral_parity driver is met by an existing product in a new form. In Feb 2034 FDA approved a 50 mg Wegovy pill on a 72-week head-to-head trial: 16.4% mean loss versus 16.1% for injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg, non-inferior, with DEXA and bone endpoints reported. This is parity with the injectable most Americans actually use, not with tirzepatide (~20%) or 12 mg retatrutide (~30%), which stay injectable. Lilly's next-generation orals are in development and unfiled. Survodutide, under review at the start, was approved Mar 2033 for chronic weight management only, and its MASH sNDA is under review with no decision. MariTide, also under review, was approved Jul 2033 as a monthly injectable at ≈17–20% loss with a 72-week DEXA statement. Neither adds a new indication. Retatrutide 12 mg came off allocation in mid-2033. Bimagrumab combinations remain in phase 3 with no filing. The smoking-cessation SHAPS trial is still enrolling. No new indication this step. Incretin market ≈$194B in 2034. US ≈$170B: ≈70.9M paying users (78.0M − 7.1M imports) × ≈$200 average net × 12. Ex-US ≈$24B and eroding.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and the leading cause of voluntary stops. Rates on the 50 mg pill are similar to injectable semaglutide, with more early nausea.
Rising in absolute numbers with high-dose regimens and the larger 65+ population.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Counterfeit and overdosed gray product confounds reporting more than ever.

A population-scale problem. ≈1.6M long-term older users meet sarcopenia criteria in Medicare claims. Lean mass is ~30–40% of loss in untrained users over 50, and the MariTide DEXA data fall in the same range.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label. Body-composition monitoring is in the retatrutide 12 mg, amycretin and MariTide labels. CMS annual DEXA requirement for long-term 65+ users unchanged.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈7.0M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. 7.0M × ~0.6%/yr baseline hip-fracture rate × 0.35 excess ≈ 14,700 excess hip fractures a year, against ~305,000 US total. The vertebral-fracture tail among cycling postmenopausal women 50–64 continues. DEXA waits have eased slightly to 10–16 weeks as mobile capacity grows.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelling retained; bone endpoints required in all filings; CMS 90-day bone-pause code unchanged; private gated plans still not bound by it. The DOJ civil case against Novo is unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded from suspected. A 2033 FDA Sentinel analysis plus pooled European registries give a relative risk of ≈1.7 across the class, higher with diabetes and rapid dose escalation. At an assumed ~4 per 100,000 baseline in a user population of ≈78M, that is roughly 2,000 excess cases a year. These are mostly partial, permanent vision loss in one eye. Absolute risk per user remains low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: May 2034: class Warnings and Precautions statement across all GLP-1 receptor agonist products (injectables, orals and low-dose oral starters), plus a Medication Guide update. Not boxed. Telehealth 'calm' brands must carry it. New MDL consolidation underway.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The 2032 retatrutide data stand: ~12% of 12 mg users versus ~5% of comparators, observational and dose-dependent. A small academic survey of 'calm' subscribers (2034, n≈2,100) finds elevated SHAPS scores but no comparator. Still no randomised measurement at low dose.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FTC consent orders stand: no 'anxiety treatment' claims, 'calm' and 'focus' permitted. No label change.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The 2033 pen shortage produced about 2M forced stops in five months, on top of gating, tenure-gap and bone-pause stops.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CMS bone-pause code softens it for Medicare; the Seventh Circuit still has not ruled on the Indiana waiver.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium and protein insufficiency are common in high-loss older users and in gray-market users with no clinical contact.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; the Part D counselling template screens for it. No FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of follow-up. The adolescent bone-accrual question is unresolved, with full data due 2034–35. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements continue; FDA adolescent data deadline 2034 partially met, extension granted to one sponsor.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now a public-health story. Imported or counterfeit users rose from ≈3.8M to ≈7.1M. Poison-centre GLP-1 calls are up ~70% since 2032, driven by dosing errors with mislabelled 'research' vials of retatrutide and tirzepatide. A Nov 2033 cluster of contaminated vials caused ≈410 hospitalisations, mostly abscesses and bloodstream infections, and 11 deaths across six Southeastern states.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CDC Health Advisory; FDA import alerts on four Indian and Chinese exporters; seizures up. The 'Safe Pens' bill still stalled. Individuals still not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. Pressed counterfeit Wegovy-pill and Foundayo tablets appeared after the 50 mg launch. Lab tests of seized lots find 0–300% of labelled content. Harms are mostly GI and hypoglycaemia in insulin users, with less infection risk than vials.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA public warning; NABP verified-pharmacy guidance; no new law.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in 65+ users with more than 2 years' use. The NAION warning adds monocular vision loss as a cited fall cofactor in a minority of cases.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening mandatory in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Worse after the 2033 forced stops. DEXA cohorts show more visceral fat and less lean mass at the same weight after repeated cycles, concentrated in over-50s cut off by gating, tenure gaps or shortage.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Joint guidance discussion; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Mean resting heart-rate rise of several bpm at 12 mg retatrutide; arrhythmia significance unclear.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Precautionary label; CV outcomes trial ongoing.

food_and_beverage.state: With about 28.5% of adults on the drug, salty-snack volume falls ~4% a year and confectionery ~5%. Private-equity candy portfolios are cutting SKUs. Fortified 'bone-forward' dairy and protein lines still lead. The new split is by price tier. Premium protein brands sell to coached top-third users, and discount grocers in Phoenix's west side and Dayton push cheap protein shakes and 'regain-friendly' calorie-dense value packs to people cycling off.

alcohol.state: Seventh straight year of spirits volume decline, with beer also down. Non-alcoholic and premium single-serve formats hold. Tobacco and vape keep falling faster than the pre-2028 trend.

restaurants.state: Traffic roughly flat, spend per cover down ~10% from 2028 in high-uptake suburbs. Gram-priced protein bowls are standard. 'Full table' weekend nights spread. Value buffets keep closing, but a handful in non-expansion rural states are recovering among people who are off.

apparel.state: Class sizing. Premium athleisure and tailoring brands cut 'structured shoulder' patterns for trained, medicated bodies and run in-store DEXA partnerships in Scottsdale and Buckhead. Discount chains carry 'cycle' ranges with elastic waists across three sizes. Mid-market brands keep shrinking plus inventory. Resale sized for cycling keeps growing.

fitness.state: Growing. DEXA-plus-coaching chains add strip-mall sites, Medicare Advantage 'prescribed lifting' expands, and mobile DEXA capacity is up about a third. The binding constraint is still staff qualified for older lifters. Premium gyms market 'regimen management' memberships at $250+/month.

insurance.state: Employer coverage dipped to 64% after the price rise, and ~85% of covering plans are gated. About a third of those now add tenure gates (coverage after 6–12 months' service, ending at separation), plus premium tiers tied to verified kiosk weights. Pharmacy trend ~+11% (volume plus price). Life insurers price untreated BMI ≥30 explicitly. Bone, fall and NAION costs land partly on Part A and Medicare Advantage.

pharma.state: Volume up ~15% and private net price up ~8%. Lilly leads on retatrutide (off allocation), tirzepatide, Foundayo and MariTide uptake via partnership ... no: Amgen sells MariTide. Novo recovers share with the 50 mg pill after its 2033 pen recall, while paying remediation costs and losing injectable share. US generic semaglutide is parked until at least mid-2035. Indian and Chinese makers win abroad and in the parcel trade. Ophthalmology clinics see a new referral stream.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Income. Whether someone is on the drug no longer tells you much, and the shape of the result does. Trained shoulders, DEXA-verified lean mass and steady weight read as a top-third regimen: 12 mg retatrutide or monthly MariTide with a coach. A lean but soft 'pill body' reads as the middle: the 50 mg pill or a gated employer plan. Visible cycling, the thin-armed stoop in over-60s, and regain around the middle read as kiosk-gated Medicaid, a tenure gap or a Hyderabad pen.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use rates still converge, with the bottom third at 24.5% against 32% at the top, but bodies diverge. In Phoenix, Scottsdale's coached users and Maryvale's import users are on the same molecule class with opposite DEXA results. The demographic most visibly sorted is women 50–64. Those on employer plans with coaching keep muscle. Those who cycled through gating and the 2033 shortage carry the fat-dominant regain pattern and are the group the vertebral-fracture tail falls on.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first shared meals are the norm among users. Hosts plan for 'on' guests. Sunday full-table dinners, church potlucks and no-gram rooms persist as heritage, and in Memphis and Houston they are increasingly where off and cycling working-class families eat out.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps keep the on/off/pausing field, and a growing number of profiles mention 'coached' or a named regimen, which users read as an income signal. 'Unmedicated' persists as a niche identity. Advice columns field complaints about partners whose gray-market pens worry them.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Medicalised and assumed managed among the insured. The backlash coalition is about the same absolute size. After the contamination cluster it gained a new argument against 'pen poverty', and it allied loosely with harm-reduction groups that hand out lot-check lists.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. The 2032 postmarketing figures stand: ~12% of 12 mg retatrutide users versus ~5% of comparators. With retatrutide off allocation, ≈8M Americans are now on top-dose triple or dual regimens, which implies on the order of 550k excess clinically meaningful anhedonia cases if the association is causal. ≈4.6M 'calm' and 'focus' subscribers on low-dose orals remain unmeasured except for one uncontrolled 2034 survey. Counterfeit 'calm' tablets, with content from 0 to 300% of label, add unknown exposure.
interior_life.framing: Feature in retail, side effect in clinic, and now an eye warning on the box. 'Quiet', 'Even' and 'Unhooked' still cost $149–199/month on the $149 oral starter doses. Since May 2034 their onboarding screens carry the NAION class warning beside the word 'calm'. Prescribers say 'reward modulation'. Users say 'the grey'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: 'Focus' subscriptions are reimbursed through lifestyle accounts at most large white-collar employers. Tenure-gated coverage makes the drug a retention tool: warehouse and call-centre workers describe staying put to 'vest' into coverage, and HR calls this 'metabolic tenure'. Sales and hospitality staff still dose down before peaks. Unions bargain over tenure gates and over whether bone-pause and NAION-workup stops count against gating.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Critics' 'grey era' label has become a marketing genre, and 'written unmedicated' is a niche badge in Nashville and on comedy tours. High-stimulus leisure (spice, volume, extreme sports, escape rooms) keeps growing. A small wave of documentary and indie film follows pen sellers and lot-check volunteers.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists screen for dose, subscriptions and gray-market sourcing. Dose-holiday weekends and 'restart' anti-nausea packs remain common. Couples counselling now often deals with one partner coached and one partner on imports, which is an income gap expressed in bodies.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Politics is about price and sourcing. The parked generic and the $50 portal rise are campaign material for 2034 midterm candidates in both parties. The 'Safe Pens' bill is still stalled between pharmacy groups who want the mail sealed and populists who want import legalised. Senior groups lobby on DEXA capacity and now on eye exams. No government action resulted this step.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding and enforcing. It added the NAION class warning, issued the warning letter that parked the first generic, put import alerts on four exporters, approved survodutide and MariTide with DEXA language, and approved the 50 mg pill on head-to-head data. It still brings no individual prosecutions, and Congress has passed no importation law or authentication law. FTC consent orders stand.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Unchanged from 2032: permanent Part D obesity benefit at the $199 statutory rate with a $50 copay; 90% Medicaid match for the 31 states plus DC on the continuation standard. No new state action and no individual mandate. Because the public rate is fixed, the 2033 price shock fell on cash, commercial and import users.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard is unchanged: ≥80% PDC, verified six-monthly weights, 5% response or clinician override, annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users, 90-day bone-pause code, and two misses suspend coverage for 6 months. Indiana and Arkansas keep their 12-month rules. The expansion is private. ~85% of covering employer plans are gated, a third add tenure gates, and premium tiers key to verified kiosk weights under the existing 30% wellness-surcharge allowance. Kiosk and connected-scale data now feed private premiums as well as public eligibility.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers toward tirzepatide. After the NAION warning, large fleets voluntarily add annual visual-field checks for medicated drivers over 50, and FMCSA has issued no new rule. Army accession policy is still contested; Air Force waivers continue.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Chinese API and Indian finished product supply the world and most of the 7.1M-user US gray market. Section 232 tariffs remain and manufacturers cite them alongside recall remediation. The US–India 'pharmaceutical parcel cooperation' language produced joint seizures but no legal channel. The import alert on the Telangana plant is now a bilateral irritant, and Indian officials call it protectionism.

events.event: FDA issues a warning letter and import alert to the first-filer generic semaglutide maker's Telangana sterile plant. Because that company holds 180-day exclusivity, no other generic can launch, and the 2033 US entry date passes with no generic on shelves. Rival filers' settlement dates fall in mid-2035

Novo recalls millions of Wegovy and Ozempic pens over sterility-assurance failures at a fill-finish site, and FDA lists injectable semaglutide in shortage for five months. Weeks later Novo and Lilly raise direct-portal maintenance prices by about $50 as the 2029 price commitments lapse, while the Medicare $199 rate holds by statute

CDC issues a health advisory after contaminated imported 'research' tirzepatide and retatrutide vials cause about 410 hospitalisations and 11 deaths across six Southeastern states. Poison-centre GLP-1 calls are up 70% on 2032, and FDA puts four exporters on import alert

FDA approves a 50 mg Wegovy pill after a head-to-head trial shows 16.4% weight loss, non-inferior to the weekly injection. Switching from pens accelerates, and pressed counterfeit tablets turn up in parcel seizures within two months
FDA adds a class warning for NAION optic-nerve damage to every GLP-1 drug label, including low-dose 'calm' subscription products, citing a Sentinel analysis with a relative risk of about 1.7

Two of the largest benefits administrators roll out 'metabolic tier' plan designs that tie incretin coverage to 12 months' tenure and price premiums off verified kiosk weights. The same quarter, a national apparel chain splits its line into 'structured' and 'cycle' ranges, and analysts call body shape the new income proxy
events.driver: coverage_shift: mandate_or_conditioning; cultural_response: class_stratification; personality_layer: marketed_feature

open_tensions: US generic semaglutide is parked behind a warning letter until at least mid-2035. Meanwhile ≈7.1M Americans use imported or counterfeit pens and now pressed pills. Congress has neither legalised import nor passed authentication, and the contamination cluster has not moved the Safe Pens bill.

The public rate is frozen at $199 while cash and commercial prices rose, so manufacturers recover margin from employers. The employers respond with tenure gates and weight-priced premiums, which turn the drug into job lock and kiosk data into a premium input, all without any new government action.

The NAION class warning now sits on the boxes of ≈4.6M 'calm' and 'focus' subscribers who have no obesity indication. No one has measured either their blunting or their eye risk, and normalisation keeps both quiet.

Medicare holds the oldest, most bone- and eye-vulnerable users at a fixed price. About 14,700 excess hip fractures a year plus new ophthalmology referrals are billed to Part A and Medicare Advantage, and no budget score counts them. The 50 mg pill makes continuous lifelong use easier just as the cycling data argue for it and the bone data argue for pauses.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is on the US market; generic_us remains false.
The permanent Part D obesity benefit still pays the $199/month negotiated rate with a $50 beneficiary copay, eligibility BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity, and the counselling visit.
The CMS continuation standard is unchanged, including the 90-day 'bone pause' code, and the same 31 states plus DC use it for the 90% Medicaid match.
The Indiana and Arkansas Medicaid 1115 waivers still end coverage for 12 months after two missed verifications, and the Seventh Circuit has still not ruled.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer direct channels.

prose.headline: The Pill Caught Up, the Pen Got Pricier, and Your Shoulders Now Tell Everyone What You Earn
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 almost three American adults in ten are on an incretin drug. Whether someone is on it no longer tells you much. What tells you something is the shape the drug left behind. Across a Scottsdale brunch table or a Buckhead gym floor, trained shoulders and a steady waist mean a coached regimen: twelve milligrams of Lilly's triple agonist or Amgen's new monthly shot, a scan every year, a trainer who knows bone. On the west side of Phoenix or in Dayton, a soft middle over thin arms means something else. It means kiosk weigh-ins, a plan that cut you off, a pen bought in a parking lot. The molecules are the same and the bodies are different.

The gap widened because prices went up, which almost nobody had planned for. Generic semaglutide was supposed to reach American shelves in 2033. Instead the FDA issued a warning letter to the company that held the first right to launch, and under the law's 180-day rule nobody else could launch either. Rival generics now wait for 2035. That summer Novo recalled millions of pens over sterility failures, and injectable semaglutide went into shortage for five months. When supply returned, the old price commitments had quietly expired, and Novo and Lilly added about fifty dollars a month to maintenance prices. Medicare did not move, because its $199 rate and $50 copay are fixed in statute. So the increase fell on employers, cash buyers and everyone in between.

Employers answered with conditions. Most covering plans were already gated by weight loss and adherence. Now a growing share also require a year on the job before the drug is covered, and they price premiums off verified kiosk weights. Benefits consultants call it metabolic tenure. Warehouse workers call it waiting to vest. There was no new law and no new federal rule. The continuation standard that governs Medicare and thirty-one state Medicaid programmes is exactly what it was in 2032.

The people priced out did not stop. They went abroad by parcel. About seven million Americans now use imported or counterfeit product, nearly double the 2032 figure: Indian generic pens at twenty or thirty dollars, Chinese 'research' vials of drugs the FDA has not cleared at those doses. In November 2033 a run of contaminated vials sent about four hundred people to hospital across six Southeastern states and killed eleven. Poison-centre calls are up by more than two-thirds. Harm-reduction volunteers now circulate lot-number blacklists on Telegram, and the authentication bill is still stuck in committee.

In February the needle stopped being necessary for most people. A fifty-milligram Wegovy pill matched the weekly injection head to head, and millions switched, many of them shortage refugees. The pill matches the shot most people use, not the strongest ones, so top-tier results still come from a pen. Within weeks counterfeiters were pressing tablets.

In May the eye warning arrived. After years of conflicting studies, the FDA put a class warning for optic-nerve stroke on every GLP-1 product, at a relative risk of about 1.7. At this scale that means roughly two thousand excess cases a year, mostly partial and permanent vision loss in one eye. The warning applies to every box, including the four and a half million 'Quiet' and 'Even' subscribers who take a low dose for calm and focus with no weight problem at all. Their onboarding screen now shows the eye warning just under the word calm. Nobody has measured what the drug does to them, which is also true of their pleasure.

The bone wave keeps rising with the older user base, now about fifteen thousand excess hip fractures a year, billed to a part of Medicare that does not pay for the drug. Everyone is waiting for 2035 again.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
At 5:40 Marisol Ortega holds the pen under the kitchen light and reads the lot number twice. The Maryvale Telegram list has forty-one flagged batches since November. Hers isn't on it. Twenty-eight dollars, from a woman who drives up from Nogales on Thursdays. She injects beside her navel and checks the box for the eye leaflet. Hers is printed in Hindi.

She switched agencies in March for two dollars more an hour. The new plan covers the drug after twelve months. September, if she lasts.

By eight she is in Arcadia, unpacking Mrs. Halvorsen's mail-order box: the new pill, a Part D sticker, fifty dollars, an orange insert about sudden blurring. Mrs. Halvorsen is eighty-one and tells her the pill is easier than the pen they took away last summer. Marisol cuts the toast into strips and pours the fortified milk.

At eleven the DEXA van is parked at the Lutheran church. Mrs. Halvorsen's scan is due. Marisol wheels her across the lot and waits on a folding chair beside a man in a golf shirt whose shoulders fill it. His trainer is texting him about his lean-mass number.

On the drive home she stops at the Fry's kiosk out of habit. She steps on, but there is no plan for it to report to. The screen thanks her anyway.

Her daughter calls from Tucson. Her company's plan covers Zepbound now, with a coach. Come visit, Mami, we'll go to the gym.

Marisol says Sunday, maybe. She buys the big tub of discount protein, and on the way to the car she looks at her arms in the window.
